name: Wayve
summary: Wayve develops end-to-end AI software for self-driving cars, backed by Nvidia, Microsoft, Uber and several automakers.
overview: Wayve builds an AI driving system that learns from data and is designed to be licensed to automakers and fleets worldwide.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Series D plus milestone capital from Uber.

bull_case: Backing from Nvidia, Microsoft, Uber and three automakers gives Wayve a clear path to deployment at scale.
bear_case: Waymo, Tesla and Chinese rivals are further along, and regulators move slowly.

metrics.note: Series D plus milestone capital from Uber

company: Wayve was founded in 2017 by Alex Kendall and pioneered end-to-end AI for driving, where one model learns to drive from data instead of relying on hand-coded rules. It aims to license its system to automakers and robotaxi fleets rather than run its own service.

In February 2026 Wayve raised $1.5 billion, including a $1.2 billion Series D led by Eclipse, Balderton and SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and milestone-based capital from Uber, at an $8.6 billion valuation. Microsoft, Nvidia, Mercedes-Benz, Nissan and Stellantis also invested.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Wayve is the leading European self-driving company and a read-through for whether licensing AI driving software to automakers can rival Waymo's approach.

changed.text: A $1.05B Series C led by SoftBank.
A $1.5B Series D values it at $8.6B.

takeaways: Automaker investors double as potential customers.
Its licensing model avoids the cost of running robotaxi fleets.
Uber's milestone capital ties funding to deployments.
Proving safety at scale is the main hurdle.
